clue.text: French philosopher's timeless stuff out of top drawer? Just the opposite

definitions.note: the possessive is carried by the name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau's

indicators.note: less time: the T standing for time is taken away from the word

parts.words: stuff out of top drawer? Just the opposite
parts.note: a trousseau is the linen and clothes a bride collects, kept in the British 'bottom drawer', the opposite of the top drawer

explanation.surface: A query about a French thinker's belongings, apparently not of top-drawer quality.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a bride-to-be's 'bottom drawer' holds her TROUSSEAU; 'Just the opposite' flips 'top' to 'bottom'. 'timeless' removes T (time) to leave ROUSSEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the Geneva-born, French-language Enlightenment thinker behind The Social Contract.

clue.text: Not liking broadcaster's pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate nickname for the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster

explanation.surface: The BBC declares that it disapproves of something.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE (the BBC) said aloud matches ANTI as many pronounce it, with a long final vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as an adjective or preposition means opposed to or against something, hence not in favour.

clue.text: Old American in Tennessee that may be full of beans

definitions.text: that may be full of beans

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the Tennessee abbreviation surrounding it

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Tennessee
the Incas were an ancient South American people

explanation.surface: An old American living in Tennessee who might be full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of beans' looks like lively character description; here it is literal, a can holding baked beans.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked beans are sold in metal containers, so such a container is literally filled with beans.

clue.text: Assembled portrayal of it, following page just released

indicators.note: the phrase 'of it' comes after the page and new-release letters in the answer

parts.note: hot means fresh, just out, as in hot off the press

explanation.surface: A description of something that has just come out, following a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A Photofit is a picture of a suspect's face built up from separate stock features, so it is a composed likeness.

clue.text: Not a tie, having broken through for province

parts.note: no means not, as in 'no good'

indicators.note: the tie has broken into the word for through, splitting it

parts.note: via means by way of, through
an ascot is a broad neck tie

explanation.surface: Someone, not wearing a tie, broke through to reach a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a tie' reads as one phrase, but 'Not' stands alone; the tie is an ascot, a wide cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's Atlantic provinces, with Halifax as its capital city.

clue.text: Block article's description of a fragmented region

parts.note: to balk is to thwart or obstruct
an is the indefinite article; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A grammar point: a blocking article describes a broken-up area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan peninsula's split into small rival states gave 'balkanise', so the adjective evokes a fragmented area.

clue.text: I'm out and wandering around top location on Greek island

indicators.note: wandering about suggests the letters move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A hiker goes off wandering around a Greek island's summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida is the highest peak on Crete, the largest Greek island, associated with Zeus's birth myth.

clue.text: A top, not very abbreviated, in cotton fabric

indicators.note: not says the very abbreviation is left out of the top word

parts.note: a vertex is the highest point, the top
V is the short form of very, as in music or 'v good'

explanation.surface: A clothing note: a top, not overly short, made of cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like a garment, which fits the fabric surface, but here it means a summit or highest point.
explanation.definitionFit: Aertex is a trademarked loose-weave cellular cotton cloth used for shirts and underwear.

clue.text: Kind of pipe that has distributed H2O over reasonable area

indicators.note: the shuffled water letters are spread over, enclosing, the other two pieces
distributed means spread around, so the formula's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the chemical formula for water gives the letters H, H and O
OK means acceptable, reasonable

explanation.surface: A pipe that spreads water about over a decent-sized patch, like a sprinkler.
explanation.walkthrough: H2O is read as its letters, two H's and an O, not as water.
explanation.definitionFit: A hookah is a water pipe for smoking in which the smoke is cooled by bubbling through a bowl of water.

clue.text: It's a west-facing wine-producing area

indicators.note: in an across clue, facing west means read from right to left

explanation.surface: A vineyard district described as having a westward aspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a town and province in Piedmont, Italy, famous for sparkling Asti Spumante.

clue.text: Rudimentary ways in which chess beginner goes on offensive, capturing rooks one by one

parts.note: the first letter of chess

indicators.note: capturing means taking pieces inside, as a chess piece is taken
one by one says the rooks are taken in singly, each going in at a separate spot

parts.note: attacks means goes on the offensive
R is the chess notation for a rook; the plural supplies two of them
R is the chess notation for a rook; this is the second of the two rooks

explanation.surface: A chess game in which a novice attacks and takes rooks one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one by one' matters: the two rooks do not go in together but at separate points, one after the first A and one after the double T.
explanation.definitionFit: Cart tracks are rough unmade paths worn by wheeled vehicles, so they are basic roads.

clue.text: Stay behind with one kept in by staff again

indicators.note: the numeral is held inside the restaffing word

parts.note: to reman is to staff or crew afresh
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Detained after hours, with someone held back by the restaffed office.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay on in a place after others leave.

clue.text: Like you or me, fudged hard option

indicators.note: fudged means botched or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone like us has dodged a difficult choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropoid means resembling a human being in form, which describes any person.

clue.text: Erasing mildly abusive word about a Conservative

indicators.note: about means around, so the swear word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: effing is a softened swear word, a euphemism for a stronger expletive

explanation.surface: Wiping out a mild insult directed at a Tory politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to rub out or remove a mark, so effacing is the act of wiping away.

clue.text: Politically diverse assembly in no-win situation, liable to fall apart

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, gathers states of every politics
tied means level, with neither side winning

explanation.surface: A many-sided assembly stuck in deadlock, on the verge of collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untied, like a parcel or knot whose string is loose, is free to come undone.

clue.text: As tax may be, having set up island — old money welcome

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island of Napoleon's exile
D stood for the old British penny
ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: Someone sets up on an island, welcoming old money that escapes tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax that can be legally avoided is evadable, able to be escaped or dodged.

clue.text: Announces conditions

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the plural noun share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to declare formally, and a state is a condition or situation something is in.

clue.text: Ostentatiously paraded a call for peace buried by opinion editor

indicators.note: the call for quiet lies inside the opinion word

parts.note: a say is a voice or opinion, as in 'have one's say'
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: An editor's opinion piece swallowing up an appeal for calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering way, so sashayed is having strutted.

clue.text: With no end in sight, ask the man why breather isn't okay?

indicators.note: each word in sight loses its end, so the final letters of the three words drop

explanation.surface: Asking a man, endlessly, why someone breathing is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters K, E and N go from ask, the and man, leaving AS, TH and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory condition that narrows the airways, the reason someone breathes with difficulty.

clue.text: Liverpool player reportedly was crossing river for epic struggles

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the name is taken by sound

parts.note: Ringo Starr, the Beatles' drummer, came from Liverpool

indicators.note: the verb was goes across, around, the river letter

explanation.surface: A footballer from Liverpool apparently swam a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liverpool player' suggests a footballer, but it is the drummer Ringo STARR, sounding like STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars is George Lucas's space-saga film series, depicting galactic conflicts on a grand scale.

clue.text: Temperature upset leaders in Haiti and another tropical island

indicators.note: the first two letters of the island name are upset, swapped round

explanation.surface: Rising heat disturbs Haiti's rulers and another Caribbean-style island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' are the island name's first two letters, which trade places; it is not a whole-word anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia, in the South Pacific within the tropics.

clue.text: Son in scanty clothing — scanty, indeed

indicators.note: the son letter sits within the other word
the scanty word clothes, wraps around, the son letter

parts.note: spare means meagre, scanty

explanation.surface: A boy in skimpy clothes, which really are skimpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or meagre, the same as scanty.

clue.text: Political allies upset about party? That's a puzzle

indicators.note: the reversed allies go around the party word
in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: the UK and the US are close allies
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Political allies fall out over a party, and nobody can explain it.
explanation.walkthrough: The allies are Britain and America, each turned upward in this down entry, with the party between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placement puzzle on a nine-by-nine grid.

clue.text: Moved suddenly like cat — concoction with cream secured

parts.note: a whip is a dessert of whipped cream or egg whites
lashed means tied down, secured

explanation.surface: A cat darts about after a creamy dessert that has been tied down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' suggests the animal, but it is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip that lashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiplashed means jerked violently, as a lash moves; a cat-o'-nine-tails is a flogging whip.

clue.text: Put hands out for old port

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give out cards to the players
second meaning: ..., a historic port town in Kent, England

explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' are cards in a game; Deal is an old Cinque Ports town on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing distributes the cards each player holds, and Deal is an ancient English harbour town.

clue.text: Section in crowd of fans give bowler a lift?

indicators.note: Section in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cricket supporters in one part of the ground cheering a bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but it is a bowler hat, raised in greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff a hat is to raise or remove it as a courtesy, so the bowler hat is lifted.

clue.text: Like court, or something happening there

definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to an atrium, a courtyard or central hall
second meaning: read as two words, a trial, which takes place in a court

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as A TRIAL; 'court' shifts from courtyard to law court.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court of a building, and a trial is the business of a law court.

clue.text: Solicitously enquire about art fakes put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks about forged artworks being released.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask after someone is to enquire kindly about their health or welfare.
